note: Eyler chaired the seven-member Judicial Committee of Associated Students in 1970-71. name: Michael Fiorella
note: The archive records Fiorella only as student regent; the sources say he held both offices. The 1973 Talisman states that under the new constitution two vice presidents were elected, one for administrative duties and one for activities, and that Charles Boteler and Mike Fiorella held them respectively; the Herald of 1 September 1972 calls him vice president for activities (https://digitalcommons.wku.edu/dlsc_ua_records/4871) and the 1974 Talisman says he was elected ASG activities vice-president in his junior year and was also student regent. He headed the Activities Committee, which booked Chicago, Jethro Tull and the Beach Boys, and he proposed raising the student activity fee to $5 a semester from the $1.50 then charged, the quoted words being his verdict on the existing funding. A caption in the same volume says he was chosen as the voting student member of the Board of Regents because ASG president Ed Jordan was disqualified for being an out-of-state student, while the volume's Board of Regents page says he was elected student representative by the student body; both statements come from the 1973 Talisman. Sources print him as Mike Fiorella.

note: LaCivita held the activities vice presidency for a second consecutive year in 1974-75; the archive records his 1973-74 term only. He ran unopposed for re-election. He chaired the ASG Activities Committee, worked to a $42,000 entertainment budget of which $27,000 went to two free concerts, and after protests over the poorly attended Doc Severinsen Homecoming concert absorbed the newly formed Student Action Committee into his committee, saying the added personnel would give him more people to back him up. Bookings were settled between him and Ron Beck, assistant dean of student affairs.

name: Rick Kelley
note: Re-elected on 6 and 7 April 1976 over Robert Tackett, 705 to 496, for a second term running the concert programme. He presided over the 6 April 1976 congress meeting in the absence of president Steve Henry. The 1977 Talisman describes him taking acts to the concert selection committee for approval and working with assistant dean of student affairs Ron Beck; the Seals and Crofts homecoming concert lost about $3,800. His surname is printed both Kelley and Kelly in these volumes and the spelling is not settled.

name: David Payne
note: The 1977 Talisman records Payne and Rick Kelley as the two officers beginning second terms in 1976-77. In the ASG supplement published the previous April he had written that the treasurer's job combined record keeping, advising Congress of ASG's financial position, and planning the coming year's budget with the other executive officers. name: Pam Keown
note: Elected on 6 and 7 April 1976 with 731 votes to Sally Chenault's 501. The 1977 Talisman lists her among the officers who came into the year with ASG experience.

name: Gerard Faulk
note: Faulk was acquitted of incompetence charges by Congress on 6 April 1976 and the Herald reported that he would conclude a two-year term in office during the 1976-77 ASG session. No later report of a successor was found in this archive.

name: Mike Pearson
note: Pearson ran the April 1977 general election and told the Herald that no one had been turned away from the polls, against complaints about long voting lines.

name: Cathy Murphy
note: Elected on 12 April 1977 with 580 votes, defeating Jim Keffer's 446. She had written for ASG's own Student Insight supplement the previous April on the second cheque-cashing centre Steve Henry and Christy Vogt obtained at the College Heights Bookstore. The 1978 Talisman caption on the ASG meeting photograph calls her simply 'vice president'.

name: Brent Shockley
note: Elected activities vice president on 12 April 1977 with 532 votes, defeating Bill Cortus's 510. He does not appear in the office in any later source found here: by 24 January 1978 the Herald was naming David Bass as ASG activities vice president. The 1978 Talisman separately records Shockley, a Scottsville senior, spending the spring semester in Frankfort as one of 18 legislative interns, working for the Legislative Research Commission; the archive found no report stating why or when he left the office.

name: David Bass
note: Named ASG activities vice president by the Herald from January 1978 and by the 1978 Talisman. He announced the signing of the Atlanta Rhythm Section and Brick for 14 February 1978, and said ASG had decided against a free concert that spring, spreading the funds instead and charging students $3.50 for all major concerts. He said mini-concerts might stop being free so that better acts could be booked, but that ASG was trying to keep them free and to hold spending between $1,500 and $2,500. He handled the Average White Band and Ramsey Lewis Trio free concert of 18 April 1978, which full-time students entered on a Western ID.

name: Gary Reed
note: Elected treasurer on 12 April 1977, defeating Georgiana Carlson 554 to 437.

name: Sharon May
note: Unopposed for secretary in the April 1977 election. The 1978 Talisman names her secretary in the caption to its ASG meeting photograph and indexes her as Sharon Gay May on that page.

name: Tricia Cook
note: The 1978 Talisman records that a College Heights Herald editorial attacking ASG for inaction cited among its examples an inner-office joke at a congress meeting declaring the day 'Be Kind to Tricia Day' in honour of Cook, interim ASG secretary. The yearbook adds that several ASG members afterwards said the actions the editorial listed were not laughable. The volume does not say when or why the office became interim.

name: Bob Tinsley
note: Tinsley chaired the seven-member judicial council that on 17 April 1978 rejected Ed Johnson's challenge to Steve Thornton's 72-vote win. The council heard more than an hour of testimony, met privately and deadlocked; Tinsley did not vote the first time and broke the tie in Thornton's favour on the second. The council's report found it could not be proven that enough illegal votes were cast to change the election, and Johnson said he would carry the appeal no further.

office: Chairman, ASG rules and elections committee
name: Gene Saunders
note: Saunders chaired the committee that ran the April 1978 election and first heard Ed Johnson's complaint. He said he had seen two poll workers wearing Thornton buttons and told both to take them off, that there was no basis to the complaint, and that his recommendation would be to allow the election. The committee rejected the protest and the judicial council then rejected the appeal.

name: John Grizzell
note: Photographed in debate with representative Brad Ford during the long ASG argument over ratifying the Student Rights Alliance petition on dormitory rules, which Congress eventually voted to support. One member argued during the debate that recognising the alliance would be a potential threat to the ASG housing committee.

name: David Young
note: Elected unopposed in April 1978, having been a representative from Ogden College that year; he told the Herald his main goal as an executive officer would be to begin a book exchange. In spring 1979 he explained the new constitution's creation of 24 separate races for the 24 representative-at-large seats on ASG congress as a way to make candidates compete head to head.

name: David Carwell
note: Elected unopposed in April 1978 and put in charge of concerts, saying he wanted more mini-concerts and fewer big shows. In the autumn he said the Indianapolis firm Sunshine Promotions met Western's three tests for an outside promoter, but shortly before the 3 November Player and Exile concert it emerged that the contract had never been signed, Sunshine having refused a $100,000 performance bond; it later posted a letter of credit instead. He also chaired ASG's lecture and concert committees. On 7 December 1978 the Herald reported colleagues' claims that he was neglecting the duties of an office that carried $800 a year, that he had missed five ASG meetings, and that lecture committee members and a Herald reporter could not reach him; president Steve Thornton said one more missed meeting would take him before the executive council to explain, and Carwell replied that much of his work was done on the telephone from home and defended his record. This archive found no later report of an executive council hearing, of any removal, or of a successor in the office.

name: Steve Shipp
note: One of the four executive officers elected unopposed in the April 1978 election; the Herald's results report names him treasurer.

name: Alice Wicks
note: Elected unopposed in April 1978. She told the Herald before the vote that she wanted to make students more aware of ASG's functions and that she was joining ASG because she wanted to get more involved in student government.

name: Victor Jackson
note: Jackson chaired the committee behind the student evaluation of faculty that ASG approved, a form called the Purdue Cafeteria System in which teachers pick questions from a list of several hundred around a common core. He said only the core questions would be made public because of printing costs, and put the cost at about $6,500 in the first year and about $5,000 a year after; the evaluations were scheduled to begin in the fall 1979 semester. He had earlier been the only black student running in the campus election for the Board of Regents' presidential screening committee.

name: John Holland

name: Connie Hoffmann
note: Announced the vacancies on Congress week after week and, on 16 October 1984, the openings on the Judicial Council as well. She signed the minutes for the year.

name: Suzie Wilkins

name: John Schocke

name: Barbara Rush

name: Chris Millay
note: Nominated from the floor and elected Parliamentarian on 2 September 1986. He was also vice-chair of the Legislative Research Committee that year.

name: Dwight Austin
note: Elected Sergeant-at-Arms on 2 September 1986 from a field of four nominations, and appointed to the Judicial Council the following week. The minutes spell the surname both Austin and Austion.

name: Dan Wooten
note: Named chair when Congress confirmed the whole 1986-87 Judicial Council on 9 September 1986, the appointment having been held over from the first meeting of the year.

note: Appointed chair on 2 September 1986 and encouraged freshmen to stand in that autumn's elections. In the previous year he had written the legislation asking for a scholarship for Bowling Green's sister city, Santo Domingo de los Colorados.

name: Bill Schilling
note: Appointed chair of Legislative Research on 2 September 1986 and also sat on the Judicial Council that year. He was Administrative Vice-President the following year.

name: Jeff Key
note: Appointed chair on 2 September 1986. On 9 September he reminded all class vice-presidents that they were required to serve on Student Affairs.

name: Bill Fogle
note: Appointed chair of Academic Affairs on 2 September 1986.

name: Kent Groemling
note: Appointed chair of Faculty Relations on 2 September 1986. He also sat on the 1986-87 Judicial Council, confirmed by Congress on 9 September.

name: Chris LeNeave
note: Appointed chair of Student Rights on 2 September 1986.

name: Bill Schilling
note: Reported to Congress on the Bowling Green City Traffic Commission and on a rise of more than 20 per cent in campus crime, and handed down to Congress an official record from the Judicial Council to be implemented at the next election. Impeachment proceedings against him were opened on 17 November 1987; on 1 March 1988 he told Congress he had been cleared by the University, that he would run for the ASG presidency, and that he would take a leave of office until after the elections.
